From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>

Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal alignment: step-ramp amendment & co-terming options

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for taking the time last week. Per our conversation I'm sending a concise set of options for Atlas's upcoming renewal (Q4 window). The team told me you prefer predictable unit economics but also want room to scale quickly in year 1. Attached is a short renewal_summary and a draft SOW for the proposed ramp. Top-level options: 

- Option A — 24-month term with staged ramp: 40% of committed capacity Y1 Q1, 70% by Q3, 100% by Y2. Includes 10% burst credits for spikes.
- Option B — 36-month term with front-loaded credits: higher discount in year 1 in exchange for extended commitment; smoother monthly billing.
- Option C — Co-term to Atlas's fiscal year (co-terming): compress/expand months to align renewals across accounts; we can offer credit smoothing and a one-time pro-rata to co-term.

Questions for you:
1) Do you have a hard constraint around co-term cutover dates (e.g., fiscal year end)?
2) Is an auto-renew with an opt-out window acceptable (we can build a 30/60-day opt-out clause)?
3) Any procurement/PO timing we should plan for?

If you'd like, we can put numbers to Option A vs B — I'll loop in finance and CS.

Next steps I propose:
- I send a one-page priced comparison for A vs B (by 06/22).
- If co-terming is required, we include a pro-rata and a short amortization schedule.

Attachments: renewal_summary_AtlasHealth.pdf, SOW-draft.docx

Cheers,
Connor O'Brien

Thanks for the clear options. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Atlas's fiscal year ends 12/31, so co-terming to 12/31 would be ideal. We would want the renewal to co-term on 12/31/2027 if possible.
- Procurement is asking for a 24- versus 36-month cost comparison, and confirmation that we can include a 30-day opt-out clause in year 2 if performance regressions occur.
- We have a hard PO submission deadline of 11/30 to hit our FY28 budget; if co-terming changes billing cadence we need explicit amortization (monthly) for internal accounting.

Attaching a redline from legal with some standard language requests (atlas_redline_0622.docx). The redline asks for: 
- SLA exception for burst provisioning during clinical cohorts
- Clarification on data retention duration in Private deployments

Can you put the priced comparison together and copy procurement + legal? If you need us to sign an LOI to lock pricing while legal finishes redlines we can discuss.

Best,
